key_insight: Structural evidence supports photoinduced lattice distortion in lead-halide perovskites, but it does not yet prove that photocarriers form large polarons or that polarons are responsible for defect tolerance.
engineering_relevance: For perovskite solar cells, claims about defect tolerance and transport should not assume polaron screening without excitation-density-resolved measurements that separate carrier-lattice coupling from intrinsic lattice softness and disorder.
method: Compare direct time-resolved structural probes with calculations of thermal lattice motion and effective mass.
Analyze how carrier-lattice coupling changes from 3D to 2D in Ruddlesden-Popper versus Dion-Jacobson perovskites.
Test lattice distortion across excitation densities spanning solar-cell conditions and ultrafast-pump regimes.
evidence_signal: The abstract cites direct structural measurements, computational effective-mass analysis, and new transport data, but notes that these results do not uniquely establish polaron screening of defects.
watch_item: High-density ultrafast experiments may overstate polaron effects relative to low-density operating conditions in real solar cells.
paper_title: Polarons in Lead-Halide Perovskites: What the Structural Evidence Does and Does Not Establish
